target_customer: Finance, controlling, procurement, supply chain and sales teams at European mid-market companies running SAP or other enterprise systems without a data team
problem: Mid-market companies run enterprise systems but lack data engineers to connect sources, clean messy data and build decision tools.
business_model: Enterprise software with forward-deployed engineers; free 24-hour pilot on customer data

founders.name: Leopold von Waldthausen
prior_employers: Palantir (about 3.5 years, led established customers in Germany, Austria and Switzerland)
previous_startups: weview (founded at 18, sold to DemoUp Cliplister)
founders.background_notes: Palantir role and weview sale from YC page and Startbase coverage; education not found.

investors: Angels including Christian Lindner, Mario Götze, Charlie Songhurst, Martin Schoeller, Robert Fink

technical_complexity.rationale: Connecting 600+ sources including SAP and generating live apps with LLMs is standard integration work with hard data cleaning parts; founders had Palantir deployment experience.

defensibility.rationale: Deep ERP integrations and forward-deployed delivery create some lock-in, but generic LLM data tools are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Founders say nobody built a Palantir-style offer for mid-cap firms; no incumbent move found in searches.

market_need_then: Founders said mid-size firms run enterprise systems with no data team and no vendor serving them like Palantir serves large firms (Startbase coverage).

branding.name_origin: A YesPress promotional profile says Zeit is German for time and ties the name to saving time; the company itself does not state this.
branding.domain_note: Uses hyphenated zeit-ai.com, not an exact one-word .com

identity.voice_and_tone: Made in Germany, GDPR and data residency emphasis

brand_strength.rationale: Name collides with the newspaper Die Zeit in search; Siemens ecosystem listing shows enterprise credibility, but no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Zeit AI is active. Palantir-trained founders reached EUR 1M ARR within twelve months with six people per the YC page and raised a seed of about EUR 5M in September 2026. Early traction came from German mid-market customers and a Siemens ecosystem listing. Risks include general LLM data tools, but no failure signal appears.
notes: Seed was reported as EUR 5M by Tech.eu and Startbase and EUR 4.3M by Startup Centrum; amount_usd left null because no USD figure was sourced. Competition list left empty: no named competitors dated near mid 2024 were found in two searches. Seedtable shows a 2024 seed entry; a job listing cites $6M raised; both unverified.
